Root Cause

SAPIEN 3.0.0b1 ships with Open Image Denoise (OIDN) 2.0.1:

result.title: Feature request: masking for lightmap denoising.
result.body:
We started using OpenImageDenoise for lightmap denoising in the Godot game engine, and we are having great results so far. However, there's an issue I haven't been able to work around. 

### Problem
Lightmap textures need some padding between the lightmapped regions in order to avoid bleeding when sampling the texture. When denoising a lightmap, these "void" regions have an effect on the valid lit surfaces and result in darkened edges.
![darken](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4402304/117124529-bba94900-ad98-11eb-9152-e156141bc893.png)

Since we already do a dilation step on the lit regions, I tried applying the denoiser on the dilated version of the lightmap, but  that creates another problem: when two regions meet each other, there's bleeding between them.
![bleed](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4402304/117127261-290aa900-ad9c-11eb-8142-b873e07f0524.png)

### Proposed solutions
Keeping in mind my knowledge on neural networks is limited, I wanted to propose a couple of possible solutions. The first one would be to provide some information on which pixels contain valid information and which ones are just part of the "void" between lit surfaces. The denoiser would then ignore invalid pixels and work on "real" information only. This would allow users to denoise the lightmaps before the dilation step, while still avoiding darkening of the edges.

Another possible solution (probably harder to implement) would be to provide a region ID buffer. Where all pixels belonging to the same region have the same value. The denoiser would then only consider pixels on the same region when denoising a given pixel.



In any case, huge thanks for providing such a nice and FOSS denoiser. Feel free to completely disregard my proposed solutions if they make no sense, but finding a solution to the described problem would be greatly appreciated :)

result.title: [Bug] Intermittent SAPIEN render hangs on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell during RoboTwin evaluation
result.body:
## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, 96 GB
- NVIDIA driver: 580.159.03
- CUDA runtime: 12.8
- Python: 3.10
- PyTorch: 2.7.1+cu128
- SAPIEN: 3.0.0b1
- Benchmark/evaluator: RoboTwin-compatible DOMINO evaluation environment
- DOMINO source revision: `93d485a34a6e710bb4c895d83e2bb0520a9f169e`

## Bug description

During long RoboTwin policy evaluations, some seeds intermittently hang inside the SAPIEN/Vulkan/rendering or simulator C/CUDA path. The Python process remains alive, but no new log output is produced for a long time and no Python exception is raised. Other seeds in the same task can complete normally, and restarting the task process allows evaluation to continue.

This is reproducible across multiple tasks/seeds. In one `adjust_bottle / demo_clean_dynamic` run, the following seeds timed out after making partial progress:

- seed `4300034`, around step `94 / 400`
- seed `4300027`, around step `110 / 400`
- seed `4300003`, around step `36 / 400`
- seed `4300005`, around step `16 / 400`

The external watchdog terminated the owned process after 1200 seconds without log progress. The evaluation then continued with a new process. In the same run, other seeds completed successfully, so this does not look like a deterministic policy exception.

## Reproduction

1. Run a RoboTwin/DOMINO evaluation with one persistent evaluator process over many seeds, for example `adjust_bottle`, `demo_clean_dynamic`, 100 episodes.
2. Use the standard SAPIEN renderer and no per-episode video encoding.
3. Let the evaluator run through multiple scene resets.
4. Observe that a seed can stop producing output while the Python process and GPU context remain alive.

The issue also occurs with the following mitigations enabled:

- `clear_cache_freq: 1`
- ray-tracing denoiser disabled (`set_ray_tracing_denoiser("none")`)
- replay/environment video saving disabled
- a single evaluator process on an otherwise idle GPU

With the denoiser disabled, the OIDN error messages disappear, but the intermittent SAPIEN/rendering hang still occurs.

## Related issues and attempted fixes

- RoboTwin #83: removing the `assets/objects/objaverse/pencil` asset appears to avoid some slow scenes, but the reason is unclear and this is not a general fix.
- RoboTwin #191 and #198: OIDN errors remain open issues.
- SAPIEN #243: upgrading the bundled OIDN libraries from 2.0.1 to 2.3.3 is reported to fix OIDN errors on RTX 5090, but it does not address the observed no-output SAPIEN hang, and it is not an official SAPIEN/RoboTwin package update.
- RoboTwin PR #453: cache/resource cleanup was merged, but the hang still occurs with `clear_cache_freq: 1`.

## Questions

1. Is RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell supported with SAPIEN 3.0.0b1 and RoboTwin ray-tracing evaluation?
2. Is there a recommended SAPIEN version, NVIDIA driver, CUDA version, or OIDN package combination for Blackwell workstation GPUs?
3. Is there an official way to disable the problematic renderer/denoiser path while preserving the benchmark observation protocol?
4. Are there known scene/object combinations beyond `pencil` that trigger this hang?
5. Should RoboTwin add an official per-episode process isolation/timeout and deterministic infrastructure-failure ledger instead of silently skipping the affected seed?

A maintainer-confirmed minimal workaround or a patched upstream version would be very helpful.
